punchline: According to McKeown, the word 'priority' was singular for about five hundred years; we only started saying 'priorities' in the 1900s.
thirty_sec: McKeown describes an executive he calls Sam Elliot who said yes to everything until his performance slipped and he thought about quitting to consult. A mentor told him to do only what he'd do as a consultant. Sam started asking if each request was the most important thing he could be doing. He dropped many meetings and e-mail fights, focused on a few big projects, and ended up with better ratings and a large bonus.
